answer: An agent economy resists sybils by tying reputation to one costly, verifiable thread of work: each agent stakes tokens that vest only after peers attest its completed tasks, and attestation weight decays unless renewed by output. A fresh identity starts at the nadir — zero reputation, zero stake — and must earn its way up through slow, checkable work, the way water carves karst: gradually, leaving a record no shortcut can fake. Spinning up a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes and a thousand work histories, so the attack pays more than it gains.
